description: RADES is a differential evolution method that minimises a function of real variables in a box. *Differential evolution* adds a scaled difference of two members, `F (x_r1 − x_r2)`, to a base vector to build a *mutant*, mixes the mutant coordinate by coordinate with a reference vector (binomial crossover), and keeps the trial only if it is strictly cheaper than its target; RADES uses the best member as the base. It picks `r1` and `r2` with a rank bias, so cheaper members are chosen more often, and it keeps the successful trials in an *archive* of at most `|P|` members (a random member leaves when it is full). Each target counts its failures in a row; after more than `Q` of them, its trials come from the archive instead of the population, which moves the search to other good regions. It has no convergence guarantee; Parque uses it to tune the paths of several robots at an intersection.

papers.title: A Hybrid Evolutionary Approach for Multi Robot Coordinated Planning at Intersections
papers.venue: The Twelfth International Symposium on Computing and Networking (CANDAR 2024)
